headline: Kai, the market stared down a 6.3 percent wholesale-inflation print and rallied anyway — yields backed off their 24-year high, and the hike bet moved out to December.
subline: Futures are mixed this morning, WTI holds near $97 on the Iran squeeze, and industrial production plus Travelers and Truist results land before the bell.
asof: Pre-market · index values are Thursday's close, deltas are this morning's futures · as of 5:25–6:40 AM ET · every figure links to a source below

items.title: PPI runs 6.3 percent; stocks rally regardless
items.sentence: Producer prices rose 1.3 percent in September — 6.3 on the year — with retail sales up 0.8 and jobless claims at 199,000, yet the Dow added 1.08 percent as the 10-year dipped below 5.04 intraday, per Saxo.

items.title: October hold, December hike: the market's new path
items.sentence: Polymarket prices a 70.5 percent chance the Fed holds on October 28 and a 78.5 percent chance of a quarter-point December hike, per The Rio Times' global briefing.

items.title: Futures mixed after Thursday's broad rally
items.sentence: S&P 500 futures slip 0.14 percent, Nasdaq 100 futures 0.56, and Dow futures edge up 0.12 in delayed quotes, per Investing.com.

items.title: Industrial production, import prices, bank earnings today
items.sentence: September industrial production is seen up 0.4 percent, import and export prices and the Baker Hughes rig count follow, and Travelers, Truist, M&T Bank and Regions report, per Investing.com's calendar and Newsquawk.

items.title: Bitcoin steadies near $82,000 after Thursday dip
items.sentence: It fell to $79,806 Thursday afternoon and recovered $80,000 within hours, leaving it about 35 percent below last October's record while October ETF flows stay net negative, per CryptoTicker and Saxo.

items.title: US says Iran blockade can continue indefinitely
items.sentence: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says Washington will keep tightening economic pressure as the naval blockade cuts Iran's oil exports and the rial weakens, per Benzinga and The Nation Thailand.

items.title: Energy ceasefire strains as refinery strikes resume
items.sentence: A White House source told Meduza that Trump expects Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refineries, and Friday's Everything Briefing roundup says Ukraine resumed those strikes after observing a three-day pause.

items.title: Midterm money floods in as Trump approval slips
items.sentence: A Fox News poll puts Trump's approval at a new low on cost-of-living strain, while Elon Musk has spent more than $276 million backing Republicans, per the Everything Briefing roundup.

items.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 4,000 deaths, still spreading
items.sentence: Government data show more than 4,000 dead in the country's Ebola outbreak, per Reuters, and Friday's roundups report cases reaching North Ubangi province on the Central African Republic border.

items.title: OpenAI cuts 2026 revenue outlook by $20 billion
items.sentence: The company now expects about $50 billion this year instead of $70 billion and has pushed its IPO to 2027, while Anthropic's $16.8 billion quarter heads toward a November listing, per Yahoo Finance citing the Financial Times.

items.title: Nvidia lines up $2 billion more for European AI
items.sentence: Jensen Huang says Nvidia has put roughly $8 billion into Europe over the past year and will unveil $2 billion in new deals within a week, ahead of GTC Berlin on October 20–22, per Fortune.

items.title: Tesla finally unveils the Roadster; shares jump premarket
items.sentence: The stock rose 4.36 percent in early trading after the long-promised sports car broke cover, per Benzinga.

items.title: AI stocks sell off, then claw most back
items.sentence: Nvidia fell 1.84 percent and ASML 5.7 before a late recovery, CoreWeave rebounded about 5 on Jensen Huang's reassurance, and Seoul's Kospi snapped back 4.11 percent overnight, per Saxo.
